The investor's designation was most likely an **unenforceable restriction**, not the offer of dedication I gave earlier, since the team note says the answer is one of the two listed options. It reads as an affirmative obligation to devote land to school construction, which courts generally won't enforce, and the school board never agreed to it before its 2009 vote. Restrictive covenant is the alternative, but I think the affirmative-obligation problem makes unenforceable the better fit.

CONFIDENCE: 50
